solves: Gives the person a date field they type in or fill from a calendar panel, in two modes: one date, or a period with shortcuts and two months, and takes part in the form that contains it.
use_when: When a form asks for a date the person types or checks in the calendar: a due date, a schedule date, the issue date of a document.
When a period whose start and end go together needs confirmation, such as a report period, a validity or a vacation: use the range mode, with Apply.
For a date the person knows by heart and that is far from today, such as a birth date: the field accepts typing, and the calendar is only on the button.
default on a common form; compact on a dense screen with a pointer; large on a touch screen, for every field of the form.
Set min and max when dates outside a window are not allowed, and unavailable for dates closed by a rule, such as a holiday.
do_not_use_when: For two single date fields for the start and the end of a period: use the range mode, which applies both dates together.
For compact on a touch screen: 28 is small for a finger; use large.
For the calendar as the only way to a date the person knows by heart: the field must accept typing, and it does.
To choose only a month, only a year, a week, a quarter or a time: those types are outside the component.
For a date grid that stays on the page with no field and no panel: use nph-calendar.
For events laid over days: use nph-scheduler.

mode.constraint: The Figma `modo`: `data única` is single, `intervalo` is range. Single is one field and one month, and picking a day applies and closes. Range is the Start and End fields, the shortcuts, two months and a footer with Apply. Reflects so a selector or the layout of the consumer can read the mode from the host. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

size.constraint: The Figma `tamanho`. The height of the field and of the calendar button: compact 28, default 36 and large 44. The compact field opens the default panel; default opens the default panel and large opens the large panel, whose footer buttons are the default size. Reflects so a selector or the layout of the consumer can read the size from the host. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

value.constraint: Single mode: the date, written YYYY-MM-DD. The value attribute is the initial value and the value of form.reset(). The piece writes it when the person picks or types a date, and fires change; setting it from code fires no event. Range ignores it. A text that is not a date that exists draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

start.constraint: Range mode: the first day of the period, written YYYY-MM-DD. The start attribute is the initial value and the value of form.reset(). The period counts only on Apply, or when the person leaves a typed field with the panel closed (D-13). Setting it from code fires no event. Single ignores it. An invalid date draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

end.constraint: Range mode: the last day of the period, written YYYY-MM-DD. The end attribute is the initial value and the value of form.reset(). The same day as the start is a valid period of one day. Setting it from code fires no event. Single ignores it. An invalid date draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

min.constraint: The first date that can be chosen, written YYYY-MM-DD. In the panel a day before it is disabled and the focus skips it; a typed date before it is an error that cites the limit (D-4); a shortcut is cut by it.

max.constraint: The last date that can be chosen, written YYYY-MM-DD. The same rules as min, on the other side.

unavailable.constraint: Property only. A date unavailable by rule, such as a holiday: a list of YYYY-MM-DD, or a function that gets one date and says whether it is unavailable. In the panel the day fades its number, takes focus and is never chosen; a typed date that is unavailable is an error (D-4). A function that throws counts as available.

label.constraint: Single mode: the visible label of the nph-field, already localized, such as Due date. It is the accessible name of the text. Without it the field renders and emits console.error in development, as nph-field does.

start-label.constraint: The property is startLabel. Range mode: the visible label of the Start field, such as Start.

end-label.constraint: The property is endLabel. Range mode: the visible label of the End field, such as End.

error.constraint: Single mode: an error sentence the screen owns, such as one from the server, shown on the field when the piece has no message of its own for it. The message of the piece wins. Filling it makes the field invalid; it is written through nph-field, below the text, with no icon.

start-error.constraint: The property is startError. Range mode: the same as error, on the Start field only. The error stays only on the field that has the problem.

end-error.constraint: The property is endError. Range mode: the same as error, on the End field only.

name.constraint: Single mode: the name of the entry in the form data, whose value is YYYY-MM-DD. Reflects because the form reads the attribute of the host. With no date, the entry is left out.

start-name.constraint: The property is startName. Range mode: the name of the entry of the start. Left out while the start is empty. Reflects because the form reads the attribute of the host.

end-name.constraint: The property is endName. Range mode: the name of the entry of the end. Left out while the end is empty. Reflects because the form reads the attribute of the host.

required.constraint: Goes to every field: nph-field shows the required mark, and an empty field is an error with its own message once the person leaves it (D-4). In the form the piece is valueMissing while the date is empty, or, in range, while the start or the end is empty. Reflects because the form and the selectors of the consumer read the attribute of the host.

disabled.constraint: The fields and the calendar button fade under state/disabled-opacity and respond to nothing; the panel does not open and an open panel closes. It wins over the error: a disabled field shows no error. Reflects because the form and the selectors of the consumer read the attribute of the host.

open.constraint: The panel is open. The calendar button and the keyboard open and close it; the consumer may set it. Opening and closing fire no event. A disabled picker, or one not connected, does not open: it is set back to false. Reflects so the page can see which panel is open.

week-start.constraint: The property is weekStart. The first column of the week in the panel. Sunday is the default and Monday is available (DSA-77 decision 8). A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

now.constraint: The date of today, written YYYY-MM-DD, for tests and stories. It sets the shortcuts, the focus on opening and the mark of today. Absent, the clock of the machine. An invalid date draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

labels.constraint: Property only. Every text the piece writes, already localized, as one object with the keys listed below as labels.<key>. It holds the keys of nph-calendar too, which the piece hands to the grid. The piece writes no word of its own. The names of the months and weekdays and the order of day, month and year come from Intl, in the language of the nearest lang, crossing shadow roots, with en when there is none. Placeholders are written between braces: min, max, start and end. With no key at all the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development. A label missing from an object that has others renders anyway and emits console.error in development, once, saying which keys are missing.

labels.previousMonth.constraint: The accessible name and the tooltip of the Previous month arrow of the grid.

labels.nextMonth.constraint: The accessible name and the tooltip of the Next month arrow of the grid.

labels.previousYear.constraint: The name of the previous arrow in the month view, which moves one year.

labels.nextYear.constraint: The name of the next arrow in the month view, which moves one year.

labels.previousYears.constraint: The name of the previous arrow in the year view, which moves twelve years.

labels.nextYears.constraint: The name of the next arrow in the year view, which moves twelve years.

labels.today.constraint: The word added to the name of today in the grid, such as today.

labels.selected.constraint: The word added to the name of the chosen day, and of each day of the period, in the grid.

labels.unavailable.constraint: The word added to the name of a day unavailable by rule in the grid.

labels.hint.constraint: The format hint, such as dd/mm/aaaa. It is the help line of each field, linked to the text by aria-describedby through nph-field, and the placeholder of an empty text. It is written by the product, not derived from the language, and is never a name.

labels.openCalendar.constraint: The accessible name and the tooltip of the calendar button, such as Open calendar.

labels.clearDate.constraint: The accessible name of the clear button of the text, the end icon of nph-input, which shows only with a value.

labels.dialogDate.constraint: The accessible name of the panel in single mode.

labels.dialogPeriod.constraint: The accessible name of the panel in range mode.

labels.shortcuts.constraint: The accessible name of the list of shortcuts.

labels.shortcutToday.constraint: The text of the shortcut Today.

labels.shortcutYesterday.constraint: The text of the shortcut Yesterday.

labels.shortcutLast7Days.constraint: The text of the shortcut Last 7 days.

labels.shortcutLast30Days.constraint: The text of the shortcut Last 30 days.

labels.shortcutThisMonth.constraint: The text of the shortcut This month.

labels.shortcutLastMonth.constraint: The text of the shortcut Last month.

labels.shortcutCustom.constraint: The text of the shortcut Custom.

labels.clear.constraint: The text of the Clear button of the range footer.

labels.cancel.constraint: The text of the Cancel button of the range footer.

labels.apply.constraint: The text of the Apply button of the range footer.

labels.period.constraint: The sentence a live region announces after a choice of a period, with the placeholders start and end written between braces, such as start to end. The two dates come in the long form of the language. A period of one day is announced as that date alone.

labels.errorRequired.constraint: The message of an empty single field that is required, such as Enter the date. It is also the message of the form when the piece is valueMissing.

labels.errorRequiredStart.constraint: The message of an empty Start field that is required.

labels.errorRequiredEnd.constraint: The message of an empty End field that is required.

labels.errorInvalid.constraint: The message of a typed text that is not a date that exists. It is also the message of the form when the piece is badInput.

labels.errorMin.constraint: The message of a typed date before the min, when there is no max, with the placeholder min, which is the min written as the field writes a date, such as The date must be on or after min.

labels.errorMax.constraint: The message of a typed date after the max, when there is no min, with the placeholder max.

labels.errorBetween.constraint: The message of a typed date outside the limits when both min and max exist, with the placeholders min and max.

labels.errorUnavailable.constraint: The message of a typed date that is unavailable by rule.

labels.errorEndBeforeStart.constraint: The message of an End typed before the Start, with the placeholder start, which is the Start written as the field writes a date.

focus.constraint: focus(options) on the host puts the focus on the text of the first field, as a click on its label does.

change.constraint: A plain event with no detail, fired by the host; it bubbles and is composed. Single: when the person picks a day, or leaves the text with a different date or an empty text. Range: on Apply with a different period, and when the person leaves the Start or End text with the panel closed and a different date. Read the value, start and end from the host. It never fires when code sets value, start, end or open, nor when the date is the one the host already holds. The input and change of the inner text, and the nph-pick and nph-month-change of the inner grid, never leave the piece.

mode.choose_when: single for one date, a due date or a schedule date; range for a period whose start and end go together and need confirmation.
do_not_combine_with: two single date fields for the start and the end of a period

size.choose_when: default on a common form; compact on a dense screen with a pointer; large on a touch screen, for every field of the form.
do_not_combine_with: fields of different sizes in the same form

panel.choose_when: The panel follows the mode and the width: single is one month; range is the shortcuts and two months; on a narrow screen the range shows one month with the shortcuts on top.
do_not_combine_with: a compact field to get a compact panel: it opens the default panel

default.changes_for_user: The resting field, by the nph-input, with the label, the hint as help and the calendar button after the text.

hover.changes_for_user: On field hover only the field border changes; the calendar button stays without background and with the light icon.

focus.changes_for_user: Keyboard focus on the text, the clear button or the calendar button shows the focus border and the halo.

focus-clear.changes_for_user: The clear button takes the focus; it exists only with a value.

error.changes_for_user: The border of the field is status/error and the message shows below it, in status/error-text, with no icon, only on the field that has the problem.

disabled.changes_for_user: The field and the calendar button fade and do not open the panel; the error is hidden, so disabled wins over error.

open.changes_for_user: The calendar button keeps the hover-active look with the solid icon and aria-expanded true, and the panel shows below the field.

shortcut-active.changes_for_user: The shortcut on the arrows or under the pointer takes the hover look of nph-option.

shortcut-selected.changes_for_user: The marked shortcut takes the surface fill and the check marker, and keeps both under the opacity when it is also disabled.

business_rules: The piece is form-associated. Single writes name, with the date as YYYY-MM-DD, when there is a date; range writes start-name and end-name, each when its date exists. Required, a typed text that is not accepted and form.reset() work as in a native field.

Validity: while a field carries a message the piece wrote for a typed text, the host is badInput, with the text of errorInvalid; with none, it is valueMissing while required and the date, or the start or the end, is empty, with the text of errorRequired. form.reset() brings value, start and end back to their attributes and clears the errors.

Each date has its own nph-field. The nph-field names and describes one control, so the control row is the internal element nph-date-picker-control, which holds the nph-input and the calendar button and hands the field contract to the input. The calendar button keeps its own name.
No input mask. The text is checked when the person leaves it, and the message comes through nph-field. The hint is the help line and the placeholder.

Typed date rules (D-4, provisional): the order of day, month and year comes from the language through Intl, with the slash as separator; day and month may have or lack a leading zero and the year has four digits; the text is written back as two digits for day and month and four for the year. One message at a time, in this order: empty, invalid, outside the limit, unavailable, end before start. Empty is an error only when required. A date with a problem is not committed and the value it replaces stays; a typed value is never reordered. Only a typed End is compared with the Start.
Single: a typed date that passes is committed when the person leaves the field and fires change. With the panel open it is committed at once and the panel moves to the date.
Range, panel open: a typed Start or End goes to the panel, moves the months to it and marks the shortcut; nothing counts before Apply.
Provisional (D-13): a typed Start or End with the panel closed is committed when the person leaves the field, even when it leaves an incomplete period, and fires change.
A click in the field is not a click outside: the panel stays open.

The panel is a surface of its own, not an nph-popover, because its widths stop at 400. It lives in the top layer, opens date-picker/panel-offset below the field, aligned to its start, flips above with the same gap when it does not fit and the room above is larger, and keeps the larger side and shrinks with an inner scroll when neither fits.
Esc closes without change. A press outside closes like Cancel. Tab after the last item of the panel closes it like Cancel; the panel is not a focus trap. What was not applied is discarded.

Focus on opening goes to a day of the grid: the date of the field, else today, else the nearest allowed day. On closing it goes back to the calendar button, the one of the End field in a range, after Esc in the panel, Cancel, Apply, a pick, the button and Tab; Esc with the focus in the field and a press outside leave it where it is.
Single: picking a day applies, writes the text, closes and fires change once.

Range: the panel keeps a draft. The first pick is the start, the second the end, and an end picked before the start reorders; the period counts only on Apply. The Start and End texts keep the period that was applied until Apply: a pick or a shortcut changes only what the panel holds, and start, end and change wait for Apply. Cancel, Esc, a press outside and Tab discard the draft.

The shortcuts are seven fixed nph-option in a listbox the date picker owns, and the product cannot pass its own. They are Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month, Last month and Custom.

Provisional (D-6): Today and Yesterday are one day; Last 7 days and Last 30 days end today and include it; This month runs from day 1 to the last day, cut by the max; Last month is the whole previous month; Custom does not change the dates and moves the focus to the grid. Picking or typing dates marks Custom, or the shortcut whose period matches; on opening with a period the matching shortcut is marked, or Custom; on opening empty none is marked. A shortcut brings the months to its start. A shortcut is disabled only when none of its days is allowed, and a shortcut partly outside the min or max is cut by the limit.
Provisional (D-8): Clear does not close the panel; it empties the selection in the panel and clears the shortcut mark at once; the fields empty only on Apply.

Provisional (D-10): a third pick starts over, the date becomes the new start and the end is emptied; start and end on the same day is a valid period; Apply stays enabled: with nothing chosen it applies an empty period, and with only the start it applies that day and the End field shows the same date; with only the end the Start takes the same date.

Provisional (D-5, D-11): the two months of a range move together and stay consecutive, with both arrows on each month as drawn; the month of the start opens on the left, the current month when empty, and with only the end the month of the end opens on the right; the focus goes to the start day, the end day or today.

Provisional (D-7): the range shows one month with the shortcuts on top when the width of the window does not fit the panel of the size in use (762 default, 874 large) plus the page margin, not at a fixed breakpoint. It is measured when the panel opens.

Provisional (D-12): the shortcut column is 192, which is 12 steps of date-picker/panel-padding; the header of the grid is 40, which is control/height-default plus space/inline-tight; the month and year cell is 84, three sevenths of the default week row. The evidence draws these measures and no token holds them.
Provisional (D-14): the page margin of D-7 is space/container-padding on each side.

Provisional (D-1, D-2, D-3, D-9): the grid draws six week rows, keeps the month and year views at their drawn size, uses text/label-sm on the weekday names and climbs from months to years as a ladder; the rules are in the sheet of nph-calendar.
Combined states: error and disabled, disabled wins; a chosen and disabled shortcut keeps its fill and marker under state/disabled-opacity; a chosen day cannot be disabled.
Every text comes from the consumer, already localized, except the order of the date and the names of months and weekdays, which come from Intl.
domain_errors: A typed text that is not a date that exists, written in the order of the language with the slash: errorInvalid, on the field, with the value it had kept.
A typed date outside min or max: errorMin, errorMax or errorBetween, citing the limit; a date unavailable by rule: errorUnavailable; an End typed before the Start: errorEndBeforeStart with the Start.
An empty required field: errorRequired, errorRequiredStart or errorRequiredEnd.
A mode, a size or a week-start outside the lists, a date property that does not exist: it draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause while it lasts.
labels with no key at all — the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
A missing label renders anyway and emits console.error in development, once, saying which keys are missing.

ai_hints: Use nph-date-picker for a date or a period in a form; for a grid that stays on the page use nph-calendar, and for events over days nph-scheduler.
Give label for one date, or start-label and end-label with mode range; the label is the name, the hint is only help.
Pass every text in labels, already localized, with the hint such as dd/mm/aaaa; the product writes the messages of the typed date and the shortcuts.
Read value, or start and end, from the host on change; setting them from code fires nothing.
Use range for a period, never two single date fields.
Use min and max for a window and unavailable for a holiday; a typed date outside them gets a message that cites the limit.
Use the same size for every field and button of a form, and large on a touch screen.
Set name, or start-name and end-name, to send the dates in the form as YYYY-MM-DD.

accessibility.semantics: Each date is an nph-field with a visible label naming the text; the hint is the description, linked to the text by aria-describedby through the field. The calendar button is an icon-only nph-button with its name as the tooltip, aria-haspopup dialog and aria-expanded true while the panel is open. The panel is a non-modal dialog named by dialogDate or dialogPeriod. The shortcuts are a listbox named by shortcuts, with nph-option as role option and aria-activedescendant on the list. A live region with role status and aria-live polite announces the chosen period. The host is form-associated.
accessibility.accessible_name: The text: the label of its field. The hint is help, never a name. The calendar button: openCalendar. The clear button: clearDate. The panel: dialogDate or dialogPeriod. The shortcut list: shortcuts. The grid and its arrows: the labels of nph-calendar.
keyboard: Tab goes through the text, the clear button when there is a value, and the calendar button; in a range, Start, then End, its clear button and the calendar button.
Enter or Space on the calendar button opens the panel with the focus on a day, and again closes it.
In the grid, the arrows change the day, Page Up and Page Down the month, with Shift the year, Home and End go to the start and the end of the week; Enter or Space on a day picks it.
In the panel, Tab goes through the shortcut list, the header, the grid, and Clear, Cancel and Apply; Tab after the last item closes the panel like Cancel and returns the focus to the calendar button.
The shortcut list is one Tab stop; Up and Down move through the enabled shortcuts, Home and End go to the first and the last, Enter and Space choose.
Esc closes the panel without change; with the month or the year view open, the first Esc goes back to the days and the second closes.
accessibility.focus: Each piece shows the focus border and the halo of its own component; the shortcut active by keyboard takes the hover look of nph-option. On opening the focus goes to a day, and on closing back to the calendar button, the End one in a range.
accessibility.contrast: The label, the text, the hint and the error message pass 4.5:1 in both themes; the error message in status/error-text measures 6.88:1 and 6.96:1. The calendar icon in color/muted-foreground measures 6.69:1 and 9.81:1 over the field, and 5.76:1 and 5.11:1 over the hover background of the button. The panel border and the divider are decorative: the shadow separates the panel in light and the background in dark. The grid contrast is in the sheet of nph-calendar.
accessibility.color_alternative: The error always brings the written message; open, the panel shows below the field and the button carries aria-expanded true; today has an outline and the chosen days a fill; the period is announced in words.

invalid_combinations: A mode, a size or a week-start outside the lists — the piece draws nothing.
A value, start, end, min, max or now that is not YYYY-MM-DD or does not exist — the piece draws nothing.
No label, or in range no start-label or end-label — the field has no name; nph-field emits console.error in development.
value in range mode, or start and end in single mode — they are ignored.
error on a disabled field — disabled wins and the error is hidden.
A compact field to open a compact panel — it opens the default panel.
Two single date fields for the start and the end of a period — use range.
anti_patterns: Two single date fields for the start and the end of a period.
The calendar as the only way to a date the person knows by heart.
Using the hint in place of the label.
Using it to choose only a month, only a year, a week, a quarter or a time.
Passing a color, a size of day or a text the piece writes itself.
Reordering a typed End before the Start, or committing a typed date that has a problem.
Writing the shortcuts in the product: the seven are fixed.
